headline: Persian Gulf Oil Flows Near Pre-War Levels Despite Trader Caution
summary: Oil flows out of the Persian Gulf in October nearly returned to levels seen before the start of the Iran war, though traders remain wary about a fragile recovery.
why: The Persian Gulf is a vital maritime chokepoint for global crude oil transport and energy supply stability.

impacts.name: Crude Oil
impacts.why: Restored shipping flows through the Persian Gulf increase supply availability and can ease upward price pressures.

why_moved: Normalization of maritime oil shipments reduces supply disruption fears, exerting downward pressure on crude prices.
